decision.title: map:merge merges into its largest map (fuzzing follow-up of 1.26)
decision.summary: map:merge starts from its first largest map and puts earlier maps' entries first through sxml_map_put_first, so folds that merge small maps into an accumulator cost O(N log N), not O(N^2).

body.p: . A fold that merges a small map into its accumulator was O(n^2): map:merge inserted every entry of every map into a new map.

item.p: map:merge starts from its first largest map L (src/function_library_map.c) instead of the empty map. With L first, it is taken as it is (no map has duplicate keys, so inserting it into the empty map meets none, under every policy). With L later, and without a duplicates function, the entries of the earlier maps are put first, last map and last entry first, through sxml_map_put_first (src/xdm_map_internal.h): an entry of an equal key is dropped and the earlier entry takes the front with its key and the combined value (use-first/any: the earlier value; use-last: the later; combine: earlier then later; reject: FOJS0003). These combinations are associative, so the result, entry order and kept key included, is the forward insertion's. The maps after L are inserted as before. A duplicates function keeps the forward order (its calls stay in F&O 4.0 order) but still takes the first map as is.
Persistent maps () number entries from 2^63: puts last count up from there, puts first down; previous_entry_stamp beside next_entry_stamp.

Cost: O(m log n) for the m entries outside L, so fold-left(1 to N, map{}, fn($m, $i) { map:merge(($m, {$i: $i})) }) and its mirror map:merge(({$i: $i}, $m)) (QT4 duplicates-maps-2) are O(N log N). map_merge_scales in tests/function_library_higher_order_test.c: folds of 10,000 steps, 3.6 s for the case under ASan (release: 320,000 merges in 1.8 s); the quadratic version took 6-18 s under ASan for 1,000. map:put in a fold was already O(log n) per step.

sources.source: map_merge_scales folds of 10,000 steps under ASan, 320,000 merges in release, and the quadratic version for 1,000
